examples.solution_text:
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so $\angle OTP=90^{\circ}$.

Using the angle sum of $\triangle OTP$:
$\begin{align*}x+90^{\circ}+62^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\x&=28^{\circ}\end{align*}$

Tangents drawn from the same external point are equal in length.
$\begin{align*}PB&=PA\\PB&=8.4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

$PT=PQ$ because tangents from the same external point are equal. Therefore $\triangle TPQ$ is isosceles and its base angles are equal.
$\begin{align*}2x+60^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\2x&=120^{\circ}\\x&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$

$\angle OTP=\angle OQP=90^{\circ}$ because each tangent is perpendicular to its radius.

Using the angle sum of quadrilateral $OTPQ$:
$\begin{align*}\angle TPQ+90^{\circ}+90^{\circ}+120^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\\angle TPQ&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$

Angles at a point sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Smaller }\angle TOQ&=360^{\circ}-240^{\circ}\\&=120^{\circ}\end{align*}$

Each tangent meets its radius at $90^{\circ}$. Using the angle sum of quadrilateral $OTPQ$:
$\begin{align*}\angle TPQ+90^{\circ}+90^{\circ}+120^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\\angle TPQ&=60^{\circ}\end{align*}$

(a) $\angle OTP=90^{\circ}$ because a tangent is perpendicular to its radius. By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$\begin{align*}OP^{2}&=7^{2}+24^{2}\\OP^{2}&=625\\OP&=25\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

(b) The radius is $14\div2=7\text{ cm}$. Again, $\angle OTP=90^{\circ}$.
$\begin{align*}25^{2}&=7^{2}+TP^{2}\\625&=49+TP^{2}\\TP^{2}&=576\\TP&=24\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

In $\triangle PAC$ and $\triangle PBC$:

$\angle CAP=\angle CBP=90^{\circ}$ (tangents are perpendicular to radii).

$CA=CB$ (radii of the same circle).

$PC=PC$ (common hypotenuse).

Therefore $\triangle PAC\equiv\triangle PBC$ (RHS).

Hence $PA=PB$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).

Let $PX=PZ=p$, $QX=QY=q$ and $RY=RZ=r$. Tangents from each vertex are equal.
$\begin{align*}p+q&=10\\q+r&=12\\r+p&=14\end{align*}$

Adding the three equations:
$\begin{align*}2(p+q+r)&=36\\p+q+r&=18\end{align*}$

Subtracting $p+r=14$ gives $q=4$. Therefore $QY=4\text{ cm}$.

examples.derivation: The tangent-radius angle is 90°. Triangle angle sum gives x=180°−90°−62°=28°. The coordinates give the stated 62° centre angle and a perpendicular tangent.
Tangents from P are equal, so PB=PA=8.4 cm. Both contact points lie on the radius-2 circle, and their radii are perpendicular to the respective tangent segments.
PT=PQ makes the triangle isosceles. Its base angles satisfy 2x+60°=180°, giving x=60°. The coordinates form the stated tangent triangle.
The two contact angles are 90°. Quadrilateral angle sum gives ∠TPQ=360°−90°−90°−120°=60°. The radii have directions ±60°, matching the marked smaller centre angle.
The smaller centre angle is 360°−240°=120°. Subtracting this and the two right angles from 360° gives ∠TPQ=60°. The diagram correctly marks the reflex arc.
(a) OP²=7²+24²=625, so OP=25 cm. (b) The radius is 7 cm; TP²=25²−7²=576, so TP=24 cm. The diagram has the required perpendicular radius and tangent and consistent 7:24 proportions.

Both triangles are right-angled at contact, CA=CB as radii, and PC is their common hypotenuse. RHS establishes congruence in the stated correspondence, hence PA=PB. The drawn contacts satisfy perpendicularity.

Equal tangents give p+q=10, q+r=12 and r+p=14. Adding gives p+q+r=18; subtracting p+r=14 yields q=4, so QY=4 cm. The triangle coordinates have side proportions 10:12:14; the stated incircle centre, radius and three contact points are geometrically consistent.
